tasks.title: Countdown iterator
tasks.statement: Define a class Countdown(n): an iterator (methods __iter__ and __next__) that produces the numbers from n down to 1 and then stops (StopIteration). For n = 0 it is empty right away.
tasks.hint: __iter__ returns self; in __next__: if self.n <= 0, raise StopIteration, otherwise decrease it and return the previous value.

tasks.title: Reusable iterable
tasks.statement: Define a class Repeater(word, times): it can be looped over many times, and each time it produces the word exactly times times. __iter__ must return a NEW iterator each time.
tasks.hint: def __iter__(self): return iter([self.word] * self.times) — each call builds a new iterator.

tasks.title: Take the first n
tasks.statement: Write a function take(iterator, n): a list of the first n elements of the iterator (or fewer, if there are not enough elements). Use next with a default value or a loop over the iterator.
tasks.hint: Try next(iterator) n times inside try; on StopIteration leave the loop.

tasks.title: First even
tasks.statement: Write a function first_even(nums): the first even number in the list, or None. Use next with a default value and a generator expression — no loop and no indexes.
tasks.hint: next((x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0), None).

tasks.title: Infinite Fibonacci iterator
tasks.statement: Define a class Fib: an infinite iterator that produces the Fibonacci numbers 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …
tasks.hint: Keep two numbers a, b; in __next__: a, b = b, a + b; return a (start with a=0, b=1).

tasks.title: Evens up to a limit
tasks.statement: Define a class Evens(limit): an iterator over the even non-negative numbers 0, 2, 4, … strictly less than limit.
tasks.hint: Keep the current number; in __next__: if it is >= limit, raise StopIteration, otherwise return it and add 2.

tasks.title: How many elements
tasks.statement: Write a function count_items(iterable): how many elements any iterable object produces (a list, a range, a generator, a file). You may not use len — work with a loop.
tasks.hint: n = 0; for _ in iterable: n += 1; return n.
